evidence.clarity: 1440: the h1 'Your photo, stitched square by square.' leans on a slogan, but the subhead says plainly what it does ('turns a photo into a cross-stitch chart in real thread colours ... Fix a blotchy cheek, swap a thread'). The next step is muddied: 'Open the beta editor' does not open a beta editor (see honesty).
evidence.fit: Meets the core ask: the on-page editor edits and recolours, and it even converts the visitor's own photo locally (I uploaded a test PNG and got 'Converted to 40 x 30 stitches using 10 threads'). Samples are original (sailboat, pear), and sellers get a dedicated dark section that is candid about undecided terms. But the main action pretends the beta editor is reachable, the seller CTA goes to mailto:hello@crossling.app, which the brief did not supply, and 'Crossling doesn't claim anything over it' partly settles the commercial question the brief says is undecided.
evidence.distinctiveness: Warm linen background with a dot texture, a heavy serif display face, a red cross-stitch X mark and stitch-rendered canvas cells (each square drawn as a thread X) give it a craft identity. The structure is still the stock kit: centred hero with two pill buttons, three numbered step cards (step 1 is a generic landscape placeholder graphic), a dark CTA band, an FAQ accordion and a closing CTA band.
evidence.proof: The editor is real and deep: Brush, Fill, Pick, Unpick, Undo, Reset, Stitches/Chart toggle, catalogue swap, fabric-count sizing, own-photo conversion and a PNG export with symbols and a thread key (I downloaded crossling-your-photo.png). At 1440 only its title row and toolbar show at the bottom of the first viewport. At 390 it starts in the second screen.
evidence.craft: 1440 is polished, with a good type contrast between serif and sans and a well-built canvas and sidebar. The probe shows 17 axe colour-contrast failures and text down to 7px (the '827 · 907 · 702' label in step art; 10.9px thread codes in the swatch strip). At 320 the header CTA overflows by 68px ('Open the bet' clipped). The 1440 stats block ('Size 4.4 × 4.4 cm (1.7 × 1.7 in)') wraps awkwardly in a narrow column.
evidence.mobile: 390: the nav links are display:none with no menu button, so How it works / For sellers / FAQ are unreachable from the header. Editor tools collapse to unlabelled 36x36 icons (Brush/Fill/Pick/Unpick/Undo/Reset), and the chips, selects and palette rows are 29–36px tall, all under 44px. The hero is a long centred text block, and the artifact begins below the first screen. Tapping a square did stitch (Undo enabled). The toast appears over the thread list, not near the canvas.
evidence.honesty: 1440: clicking 'Open the beta editor' scrolls to the on-page demo and only then shows the toast 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The disclosure comes after the click, and the FAQ admits the demo uses 'a short sample of the range', so it is not quite the real thing. The invented hello@crossling.app address is used for the seller and contact links. 'Free while in beta' and 'The ones we keep getting' (implying a stream of user questions) are not in the brief. On the good side, 'Both sample patterns are drawn by us' sits directly under the editor.
evidence.interaction: At 1440 I operated every control. A palette pick plus a drag-stitch moved the 321 count from 17 to 25. Undo enabled. Swap opened the catalogue and replaced 321 everywhere with 310 Black (toast 'Swapped 321 for 310 Black'). The Chart view shows symbols. The Pear sample loaded. Photo upload converted. Fabric 18-count updated the size to 5.6 × 4.2 cm. Export downloaded a PNG. Arrow+Enter stitched from the keyboard. No console errors. The mobile nav is missing, and feedback comes through a bottom toast away from the canvas.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the stitcher's world: 'Fix a blotchy cheek, swap a thread you don't have, drop the colour count before you buy floss', 'A chart is only useful if the shop sells the colour', 'costs you a skein for a handful of stitches'. It is undercut by the CTA label promising a destination it doesn't have and by 'the editor below is the real thing' contradicting the FAQ.
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: eyebrow, slogan h1, subhead and two buttons fill the viewport, and only the editor toolbar peeks at y≈690–900, with no pattern visible. 390x844: headline, subhead and CTA only, with no artifact in view. The action label ('Open the beta editor') does not match what happens.

problems: The primary CTA 'Open the beta editor' (header, hero, closing band) only scrolls to the on-page demo and admits this in a toast after the click, so the label promises a destination the page cannot reach.

The mobile layout is a shrink, not a recomposition: no menu at 390 (nav hidden, no toggle), unlabelled 36px tool icons, the artifact below the first screen, and a 68px horizontal overflow at 320 that clips the header CTA.
The first screen is a generic centred hero with the product artifact pushed below the fold, plus craft debt (17 contrast failures, 7px text) and an invented contact email for the seller path.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The most prominent first-screen action is labelled 'Open the beta editor' (header and hero; repeated in the closing band). It does not open any beta editor: app.js has BETA_URL '' and the click handler calls preventDefault, scrolls to the on-page #editor demo and only then shows the toast 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The label names a destination it does not reach, and the real result is disclosed only after the visitor acts.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/A/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Click the red hero button 'Open the beta editor'. The page scrolls to the 'Try it: a pattern you can edit' section on the same page, and a dark toast appears at the bottom with the text above. No new page or editor opens. The header and footer-band buttons with the same label behave identically.

evidence.clarity: The h1 'Turn a photo into a cross-stitch pattern, then change any stitch.' plus the lead ('a pattern editor for cross-stitchers ... real thread colours you can edit square by square') says what, for whom and what to do. The CTA 'Try the sample editor' names exactly what happens.
evidence.fit: The editor is the hero at 1440, so the canvas is the product as the brief asked. The sample is an original drawn pear, labelled 'Sample only: the source is a drawing, not a photo'. Sellers get a real column ('Making patterns to sell': chart view, live thread counts), and commercial use is 'Not decided' in both that column and the pricing table. The missing beta address is handled in the closing section: 'its link will sit here when it does'. The demo cannot take the visitor's own photo or export, which is a weaker resolution of the 'photo to pattern' promise.
evidence.distinctiveness: The editor-in-hero and the 'same picture at 12, 22 and 40 stitches' section with fabric-count sizes come straight from the product. The visual language is otherwise neutral: a light grey page, a grotesk display face, square black-bordered buttons and one red CTA. With the logo removed it reads as a well-made generic utility rather than a cross-stitch brand.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the whole operable editor is in the first viewport, beside the headline. The 4/7/10 thread buttons re-chart live, and the size figures are internally consistent (22 st = 4.0 cm on 14-count, 3.1 cm on 18-count; 12/40 st in the sizes section match the stitch ÷ count formula). The sample's background stitches (3752 very light antique blue, 331 of 484) overpower the pear, so the showcase pattern reads washed out.
evidence.craft: No axe violations, smallest text 13px, no overflow at any width. The spacing rhythm is consistent, and section rules and the pricing definition list are tidy. The weaknesses are a plain, default-feeling palette and buttons; a large dead area under the hero copy in the left column at 1440 (y≈600–790); Undo/Start over orphaned on a right-aligned row; and the low-contrast pear sample.
evidence.mobile: 390: the 'Menu' button (69x44) opens a full nav, labelled 'Close' when open. Tapping 'Pricing' closed the menu (aria-expanded false) and scrolled to the section. The h1, lead and CTA (213x48) are in the first screen, with the editor card header and 4/7/10 controls starting at y≈575. Tools are 40px tall, and swatches are 36px (slightly under 44). It was recomposed rather than shrunk: tools move under the grid, and the thread list stacks. At 320 there is no overflow. The status line sits below the thread list, away from the grid.
evidence.honesty: Every example is labelled at the point of use ('Sample only: the source is a drawing', 'Counts come from this sample', 'shades on screen are approximate'). The CTA says 'sample editor' and the aside says 'runs here in your browser on a sample picture' before the click. Commercial use is 'Not decided'. There is no invented email or contact. The only unbriefed claim is 'The beta is free to use', which is shared with A.
evidence.interaction: All three widths: stitch by drag ('Stitched row 5, column 5 in 433 Medium brown'), Swap colour ('Swapped 20 stitches of 435 Very light brown for 433 Medium brown'), Unpick, Undo ('Undone.'), More threads (33 catalogue threads; picking one adds it to the list), 4/10 re-chart ('Your edits were cleared; Undo brings them back'), Chart symbol view, Start over and keyboard arrows+Enter. The CTA focuses the grid. No console errors. The live status line is well written, though at 390 it sits far below the canvas. There is no photo input or export.
evidence.copy: Plain, specific and consistent: 'A stem, an eye, a whisker: averages lose small things', 'Drop threads you don't own, swap a shade for one in your box', 'every square in it was placed on purpose. Thread counts update as you edit, so the list is right when you ship.' The status microcopy is written, not defaulted. A few headings are long and flat ('The beta is free to use while pricing is worked out').
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: headline, lead, 'Try the sample editor' and the full operable pear editor with thread list are all in view, so the promise is specific and backed. 390x844: headline, lead, CTA, its honest aside, and the top of the editor card (title, 'Sample only' label, Stitches/Chart, 4/7/10) are in view. The grid itself starts just below the fold.

problems: The visual identity is generic: grey page, grotesk type and square black-outlined buttons. Nothing but the canvas says 'cross-stitch', and the page would not be recognisable without the logo.
The showcase pear is washed out because the pale background thread (331 of 484 stitches) dominates, so the hero artifact looks muddy next to the crisp headline.
The demo cannot take the visitor's own photo or export a chart, so the 'photo to pattern' half of the promise is only described, and at 390 the status feedback sits well below the grid.

reason: B puts the operable editor in the first screen beside a clear promise, labels everything honestly where it appears, and is recomposed properly for the phone with a working menu. A has the richer editor (own-photo conversion, export) and the warmer craft look, but its primary CTA promises a beta editor it cannot open, its first screen is a stock centred hero, and its phone layout loses navigation and overflows at 320. A version of A with an honest CTA label, the editor pulled into the first screen and a mobile menu would change my mind.
